what: Which part of the route makes the difference: the same corrector with IAS15 alone for every piece, with reg.js for every piece, and with the Dormand-Prince integrator alone at the tolerances 1e-9 and 1e-11, from the starts of the two deep stretches of fd-comparison.json; the cost of the 50 digit single shooting against the stored traces per unit of lam and of arclength. The options --pieces-by=ias|reg (tools/family-follow-ias.mjs) and --newton-tol=X, --stop-below=X (tools/family-follow.mjs) are off by default; without them every output is the same as before.
commands: node tools/dp45-attempts.mjs OUT.json -1 120 U1 U2 LAM T LABEL PIECES --stop-below=0 --newton-tol=1e-9|1e-11   (U1 U2 LAM T: command_line_start of start-shift.json for t35m and t44m; the tool is family-follow.mjs with the record of every attempt)
node tools/reproduce-trace.mjs t35m OUT.json --stop-after=31   and   node tools/reproduce-trace.mjs t44m OUT.json --stop-after=40   (the default rows)
python tools/reclose.py JOB.json OUT.json --minutes 60   (the point of step 10 of the reg run of t35 -, of step 34 of that of t44 -, ref = their own u1, u2, t)

t35m.runs: 31 recorded points from the replay start (52 accepted steps with the default route)

t44m.runs: 40 recorded points from the command-line start (59 accepted steps with the default route)

notes: The cost rows are computed from files of this folder (extra/cost-comparison.json, extra/creep-attempts.json, reclose/*.json, extra/reclose-continuation-beyond.json, extra/handover.json, traces/*.json): arclength is the sum of the Euclidean distances between successive points in (u1, u2, t, lam), lam range the net change of lam, the seconds are those of the files (the steps of the 50 digit continuations are the ones they were run with, dlam 1e-5, and the seconds per unit lam of a continuation depend on that step).
A run passes the deepest step if its last accepted step has a number above that of the deepest step of the stored trace (steps are numbered by loop step, failed attempts count).

The default rows are the exact runs of fd-comparison.json; the wall times of runs made at different times and loads differ: the same default run took 336 s (t35 -) and 816 s (t44 -) there and 162 s and 326 s when it was repeated beside the others of this file, bit-identical both times. The reg run takes 166 s and 241 s: it calls reg.js once per piece with the derivative, where the default route also calls it without the derivative on every unflagged piece for the missed-flag check.

With --pieces-by=ias the missed-flag check (reg.js on every unflagged piece) does not run, because it would run reg.js on every piece; the guards on the IAS15 analysis stay on. Counters: pieces_by_counters.

tools/family-follow.mjs stops at a closest approach below 0.03 after the point is recorded; both starts have a closest approach far below that, so the Dormand-Prince runs use --stop-below=0 (the stock rule ends the run after one accepted step, the last row).

The step lengths, iterations and residuals of the Dormand-Prince runs are those of the record of every attempt (tools/dp45-attempts.mjs); a run that stops at the first gate, the move of the start onto the family (a residual below 1e-9 of the closing equations with the Dormand-Prince flow), has no attempt.
